text:
talia: quick heads-up — Cassini LoRA merge (PR #4923) landed to staging. I ran a 1k-turn eval on raptor-int8 and int4; int8 ✅, int4 shows token drift on invoice amounts. sample: "Total: 1,200" -> "Total: 1,200.00.00"

maya: ugh. can you paste the diff? maybe tokenizer mapping got re-ordered during merge.

talia: diff snippet:
```
- special_tokens_map = {'<amount>': 50234, '<invoice>': 50235}
+ special_tokens_map = {'<invoice>': 50235, '<amount>': 50234}
```

jeff: that ordering shouldn't matter normally but quant kernels can be sensitive. Running small suite now on dedicated-gpu-3 (int4 profile). kicking off @infra-bot job: eval/cassini-int4/7123456790

infra-bot: job queued: eval/cassini-int4/7123456790 — ETA ~7m

sam: FYI we had a similar drift with Velum — root cause was LoRA merge applying adapter weights before tokenizer remap. check merge order: merge.py line ~88. Also verify KV cache alignment when quantized.

maya: running n=200 sample golden prompts. will post pass/fail counts.

talia: thanks. if we confirm it's merge order I'll revert and reapply using --safe-merge flag.

infra-bot: job started on dedicated-gpu-3.

maya: results: 200 prompts -> int8: 199/200 match baseline; int4: 162/200 match; failures are amount formatting and occasional extra punctuation. attaching quick stats: F1-like: int8 0.98, int4 0.83

jeff: that's consistent with a tokenization remap causing shifted positions. can you run a debug with `--trace-tokenization` and sample failing prompt id 47?

maya: ran trace. output:
```
prompt 47 tokens: [101, 50235, 4021, ...]
merged adapter shift at token 2 -> kv_offset +1
```

talia: ok action items:
- jeff to add remap step to merge pipeline (PR request)
- maya to run re-merged pack with `--safe-merge` and re-eval
- ops to reserve 1x dedicated-gpu for 20m for re-run

sam: I'll open rollout freeze until we have pass >= 195/200 on int4.

maya: ack. starting re-merge now.

talia: thanks all. Will ping customer if we need a hotfix. :handshake:
